headline: Learned models add spatial scale and modality as explicit inputs to omics profiling
label: Spatial Omics Representation Learning
summary: Spot-resolution and histology-linked spatial omics data are now modeled with foundation and multi-task methods spanning scales and modalities.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations of spatial omics data in which position, resolution, or modality is an explicit model input. CancerSTFormer pairs transcriptomic foundation models at 50 um and 250 um scales for niche modeling and perturbation analysis. FlashDeconv applies leverage-score sampling with sparse spatial regularization to deconvolve 1.6M Visium spots. SuperFocus generates whole-slide single-cell spatial multi-omics from spot-based measurements and histology, and STAX unifies domain identification, slice integration, spot completion, and denoising in one multi-task platform. SpaceTrooper scores per-cell quality from expression and morphology in imaging-based data, and SpatialZ generates virtual slices to build dense 3D atlases. What is new is explicit handling of scale and modality, most clearly in CancerSTFormer's two-scale design. The remaining items, including the cfDNA multimodal transformer and single-cell tools, are adjacent rather than spatial.
